CoreWeave initially loaded up on GPUs to mine Ethereum, made money during the boom, then pivoted to being a GPU cloud, and found themselves with all these GPUs in the ML/AI bubble. Amazing run.
Mining used consumer GPUs which are not allowed to be used for datacenters. So I doubt they managed to reuse the hardware.
No mining GPUs are in their fleet anymore, that's long gone. It's all datacenter GPUs as per their website.

From CoreWeave's S-1: 'For the years ended December 31, 2023 and 2024, our largest customer was Microsoft, which accounted for 35% and 62% of our revenue, respectively.' Commenter: 'I didn't know they were basically a MSFT subsidiary.'
Referenced news that Microsoft drops some CoreWeave services ahead of its $35B IPO.
In its third quarter earnings, CoreWeave reported $51.9 million in operating income — and $310 million in interest expense, prompting alarm in discussion ('Holy cow.').

Concern raised that CoreWeave uses SPVs (special purpose vehicles) for financing that 'aren't subject to the same kinds of regulations as the parent company,' questioned as a risky/unique feature of the AI spending boom.

Job candidate described CoreWeave's interview process as 'very YC-ish,' recounting three interviews for two different roles with textbook-style questions, ultimately not receiving an offer despite feeling more knowledgeable than the interviewer.

Explanation of Nvidia's $2B investment into CoreWeave for a 9% equity stake, noted to be only 5.7% of CoreWeave's ~$35B 2026 capex, with the rest of financing coming from other sources — used to argue the deal isn't purely 'circular.'
Backblaze announced a five-year multi-exabyte storage agreement with CoreWeave; Backblaze stock rose 38% on the news.
